properties.description:
When a choice is put to the user, the agent's reading travels with it: the recommended answer, why, and the condition under which the other option wins. The decision stays with the user — no status moves on a recommendation alone.

THE SHAPE IS PART OF THE CAPABILITY, added 2026-07-31 on Anthony's word after the pattern was used on him for the five standing gaps and he asked for it to be CEMENTED rather than repeated. Three separable obligations: the options are SELECTABLE rather than buried in prose, so the user picks instead of composing a reply; the RECOMMENDATION IS FIRST and marked as such, because an unordered menu makes the user infer which one the agent favours — the very analysis req:no-se-knowledge exists to spare them; and EVERY option carries its consequence, including the ones not recommended, because a list of bare labels looks complete while withholding what each choice costs.

THE LANGUAGE IS THE USER'S, NOT ENGLISH. Anthony's words: "with agents able to understand multiple languages, the 'simple english' should be 'simple whatever_language_user_is_writing_in'." The plainness obligation is about REGISTER — no jargon, no node ids, short sentences — and register is language-independent. cap:surface already says "in the user's WORDS"; this makes the wider reading explicit so nobody implements it as an English-only rule. Every English phrasing in the design notes is an example of the register, never a specification of the language.

DELIBERATELY A NEW CAPABILITY RATHER THAN AN EXTENSION OF `cap:surface`. That capability is `verified` for what it does — turning a gap into a question in the user's words — and widening it would repeat the BL-106 defect exactly: a capability is not one behaviour, so adding a second one behind an existing passing check makes the check cover less than it appears to. New behaviour, new capability, its own check. The same argument is why the shape and language obligations land HERE and not back inside cap:surface.

WHAT IS TESTABLE AND WHAT IS NOT, stated so the check does not overclaim: whether a recommendation is GOOD, and whether the language was correctly matched, are semantic judgements and stay evidenced by trials (docs/sharpening.md — deliberately no LLM evals in CI). What IS mechanically checkable is the contract: that the skill states all three shape obligations and the counterweight rule; that it states the language rule in language-independent terms; that no served text hardcodes English as the answer language; and that no requirement status, decision status or gap acknowledgement is ever written in the same act as a recommendation.

SCOPE WIDENED BY THE SAME REQUEST: this began as a rule about GAPS, and Anthony's framing — "the decisions I need to make" — is broader. Read as covering any point where the agent puts a CHOICE to the user, not only where detect_gaps produced it. Whether that widening deserves its own capability is left open in req:a-question-arrives-with-a-reading rather than assumed here.

Governed by `req:a-question-arrives-with-a-reading`. PLANNED, scheduled `expected` for rel:v0210.
properties.name: A question arrives as options the user can pick, recommendation first, in their own language
